title: TIME JUMP: 09:00 Thursday, After Landfall and the Ground-Floor Flood

fields.scenarioTitle: Clearance Time — Evacuation Decision & Vertical Critical-Care Moves
fields.narration: EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE. It is now 09:00 CDT, Thursday, September 17, 2026. Here is what has happened since the Vertical Evacuation order at 05:30 Wednesday. Tropical-storm-force winds reached Corpus Christi at 12:00 Wednesday. Coastal AirCare 2 stayed grounded, and TxDOT closed the causeways and the US 181 bridge. Hurricane Quinlan made landfall at 15:40 Wednesday as a Category 3, just south of the city. At 20:00 Wednesday surge water came in under the ED ambulance doors. The ED moved its patients and crash carts to the second floor. The main pharmacy and imaging, both on the ground floor, were cut off. The command center left floor 1 and moved to the Boardroom on floor 5, extension 4520. The NICU, 12 infants, is on 7 West. The ICU is on 6 West. Both units are still at one nurse to three patients, apart from one-to-one for the ventilated infants. We are now going back to landfall night. The next events come from the overnight logs, call records and messages, starting at 20:15 Wednesday. Play them in the order they happened and tell us what command did. The first item is a text the Facilities Director, Wesley Pruitt, sent to the Boardroom at 20:11 Wednesday. A photo was attached showing a yellow staff gauge zip-tied to the ED canopy post. The text reads: 'Water at ED entrance reads 18 inches and rising about 3 inches every 20 minutes. Pharmacy door sill is under. Generators on the 2nd floor mezzanine are dry and carrying full load, fuel at 81%. Gusts outside 85 mph.'
worldState: Tropical-storm-force winds arrived at 12:00 Wednesday, September 16. Quinlan made landfall at 15:40 Wednesday as a Category 3, just south of Corpus Christi.
Coastal AirCare 2 is grounded. The causeways and the US 181 bridge are closed, and no ground or air transfers are running.
Surge water entered under the ED ambulance doors at 20:00 Wednesday. At 20:11 it read 18 inches at the ED entrance and was rising about 3 inches every 20 minutes.
The ED is running on floor 2 with its patients and crash carts. The main pharmacy and imaging on the ground floor are cut off.
The command center is now the Boardroom on floor 5, ext. 4520. Satellite phones and radio channel 2 (command) and channel 3 (nursing) remain available.

The generators on the second-floor mezzanine are dry and carrying full load, with fuel at 81% at 20:11 Wednesday. The 2 generator-powered elevators are held for patient movement only and staffed by security.
The NICU's 12 infants are on 7 West. The ICU is on 6 West, apart from any patients command chose at 06:30 Wednesday to keep on floor 3 with a vent team.
Staffing is 1:3 on both units, with 1:1 only for the ventilated NICU infants. The 14 Gulf Nurse Staffing RNs never arrived.

The command cycle still applies: operational period briefings at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00, unit status reports to the House Supervisor on the hour, Facilities reports every 2 hours, and a PIO statement every 6 hours or after a major change.
No unit returns to its home floor until winds have stayed below 34 knots for 2 hours and inspections are done.
fields.facilitatorNote: Before you read this card, adjust the ICU census on 6 West for the players' 06:30 Wednesday decision on Beds 3-07 and 3-14, and for any patients transferred overnight Tuesday. Then say aloud how many ICU patients are where. Read the Facilities text word for word, show the gauge photo if you have one, and then begin the 20:15 Wednesday replay.

instructorNote: This card moves the room into landfall operations and the night of the ground-floor flood. Check that the IC confirms the Boardroom (ext. 4520) as the command center and the ED on floor 2, that the HS restarts the hourly unit status reports and the master tracking board, and that the CNO confirms ratios and escalates the 1:3 coverage instead of accepting it as normal.
